messages.author: 9a25c34b3581b87f
messages.subject: Suitability prediction and RSF questions
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am currently working on generating a suitability map using the mean() object from my individual models, and I have encountered several questions.

Questions related to rsf.selection()
I first performed rsf.selectiton() on my data set, and I found three individuals had abnormal ΔAICc outputs - one individual had NaN values for all models, another exhibited normal ΔAICc values for the first 10 models and Inf thereafter, and the third individual returned Inf for all models except for ~ 0. I am curious about the potential reasons for these values.
Additionally, while I understand that we can obtain the best model for each individual using rsf.selection, I am interested in knowing if there is a method to identify the best model among all individuals (i.e., for the entire population).

Questions related to mean()
I used the rsf.fit results of the global model to perform mean() due to the memory restriction on my device. However, I noticed that the output did not include some of the variables originally specified in the global model. Here are my questions:
1. Why does the mean() function automatically exclude variables?
2. Is there a way to specify the variables for suitability prediction?
3. The selection of categorical data (forest; please find below the output of summary(mean)) does not make sense to me. Why did it not select all with the same reference category (i.e., why not forest.1_0 but forest.0_1 here)?
   - forest.3_0 (1/forest.3_0)
   - forest.2_0 (1/forest.2_0)
   - forest.0_1 (1/forest.0_1)

Questions related to suitability()
I tried to perform suitability prediction using the provided code:
temp_suit <- suitability(R=R,
                         CTMM=mean_temp,
                         grid=env_all_eqd_akdescale[[3]])
However, I encountered the following error message: Error in R[i, ] : subscript out of bounds. I was wondering what might be the problem?

I am sorry for so many questions. Any insights from you would be greatly appreciated. Thank you very much!

Best regards,

Fang

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Suitability prediction and RSF questions
parts:
Hi Fang,

Unlike AIC, AICc can potentially return infinite or NaN values if the number of parameters is not sufficiently larger than the number of data points (or effective-sample-size with rsf.fit). I suspect that is what you are getting, especially given that your species tends to have small effective sample sizes. I would try BIC and if that doesn't work, then please send me a minimal working example to check.

mean() is coded up to provide a meta-analytic model for the population (and I just pushed a fix for that function for when the individual models vary). But you shouldn't expect one best individual model for all individuals, because, all else equal, the sampling can differ.

rsf.select() can drop variables at the individual level, but mean() should then keep all of the variables in the individual selected models (though not all parameters will support estimation of the population variance). If that's not the case, then please send me a minimal working example to diagnose.

You can supply different rasters for the suitability predictions than you did for the model fitting... if that's what you are asking?

I haven't yet coded up the categorical regression to be smart at the population level. Currently, you need to manually select the same reference category for each individual. But that may not be possible if there is no single category that all individuals sample from. At some point, I need to code up the mean() function to automatically transform between reference categories. If you need that functionality now, then please let me know and I will prioritize it.

For the error, please send me a minimal working example and I will take a look at it.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Suitability prediction and RSF questions
parts:
Hi Fang,

Sorry for the delayed response, I'm teaching a new population ecology class.

There is a reference argument in rsf.fit() (which rsf.select will pass).  reference="auto" will choose the most frequent category as the reference category, but mean() currently requires the reference categories all to be the same. I can code up mean() to transform between reference categories automatically if and when someone needs that, which would be the case when there's no common category across individuals, as the reference category needs to be a used category.

Best,
Chris

Hi Fang,

Unlike AIC, AICc can potentially return infinite or NaN values if the number of parameters is not sufficiently larger than the number of data points (or effective-sample-size with rsf.fit). I suspect that is what you are getting, especially given that your species tends to have small effective sample sizes. I would try BIC and if that doesn't work, then please send me a minimal working example to check.

mean() is coded up to provide a meta-analytic model for the population (and I just pushed a fix for that function for when the individual models vary). But you shouldn't expect one best individual model for all individuals, because, all else equal, the sampling can differ.

rsf.select() can drop variables at the individual level, but mean() should then keep all of the variables in the individual selected models (though not all parameters will support estimation of the population variance). If that's not the case, then please send me a minimal working example to diagnose.

You can supply different rasters for the suitability predictions than you did for the model fitting... if that's what you are asking?

I haven't yet coded up the categorical regression to be smart at the population level. Currently, you need to manually select the same reference category for each individual. But that may not be possible if there is no single category that all individuals sample from.
